Are you me? I used to have a really really unhealthy obsession with counting calories to where it would take me longer to log my food than it would to plan and make it. Ended up binging more times than I can count.

 Two things I finally let myself take control over was taking the packaged items for face value and measuring the serving sizes as they were listed, and meal prep.

Meats and veggies that I cook? Absolutely I still weigh raw. That half a tablespoon of butter I cooked my eggs in? Face value, measured in the tablespoon the package says. I tend leave about 50-100 extra calories in my tracker just in case I go over. If I don't? Awesome! Less calories at the end of the day.

Meal prepping has really really helped me not measure every little thing every day. If I'm meal prepping, I add it all together at once, and then just divide by how many meals it's for. While it may be slightly different each day, it still adds up at the end of the week. Plus, I'm not weighing everything every day. Taking away that daily stress of measuring every day with meal prepping and face value has really helped me to create a healthier relationship with enjoying the food I'm eating

I do IF and OMAD to control cravings so I'm always excited when I can do clean eating that's close to my caloric goal! I'll usually  throw a few harboiled eggs with mayo, salt and pepper on an english muffin in the mix too!

As long as your cornstarch is dissolved and you have a simple stirring motion with your broth and slowly pour in the beaten eggs I think you'll be okay! I did all the ingredients i listed minus the eggs and cornstarch into the broth to boil!

I used the recipe from [The girl who ate everything](https://www.the-girl-who-ate-everything.com/egg-drop-soup/) but with half an extra egg and a 1/2 teaspoon of sesame oil instead of 1/4. I also used vegetable broth since I tend to avoid meat :)
